newsitem.title: USA: Jury chosen in U.S. trial of ex-MGM head Parretti.
newsitem.headline: Jury chosen in U.S. trial of ex-MGM head Parretti.

text.p: The trial of Giancarlo Parretti, former owner of movie studio Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer Inc, on perjury and evidence-tampering charges began Monday with the completion of jury selection.

Parretti, who lost control of the studio in 1991 to his bankers in a Delaware court case, is charged with doctoring a bank document submitted as evidence in the earlier case to make it look as though it had been sent to him.
But Paretti's attorney maintained his client's innocence Monday and expressed confidence he would be vindicated.

"We intend to show that he never swore falsely at the trial and that the state will be unable to demonstrate that he had any knowledge that the fax tag was not genuine," attorney Eugene Maurer told Reuters.
Opening arguments in the Delaware Superior Court trial, scheduled to last four weeks, were postponed to 10 A.M. Wednesday.
Presiding Judge Richard Cooch was to first resolve a dispute over whether Parretti's lawyers in the earlier Delaware civil trial could be subpoenaed to testify in this case.
In 1991 Parretti lost control of MGM to Credit Lyonnais Bank Nederland NV (CLBN), which financed his $1.3 billion buyout of MGM, after a highly publicized trial in the Delaware Chancery Court.
CLBN, formerly a unit of France's Credit Lyonnais, has since been taken over by Belgium's Generale Bank and renamed Generale Bank Nederland.
Shortly after the trial ended, CLBN's lawyers alleged that the Italian financier had knowingly submitted as evidence a bank document doctored to look as if it had been faxed to him.
